instructions: Follow docs/content-wave-2/prompts/dedupe.md. Review every planned stub of every topic in the item against each other and against the existing inventory. Answer with the findings; an empty list when nothing needs fixing.

items.text:
Planned stubs (stubId | topic | level | type | angle | answerHinge):
- architecture-01 | architecture | middle | open | Asks what an anemic domain model is, why entities with only getters and setters plus service classes holding all rules is a problem, and when it is still acceptable. | In an anemic model the behaviour and invariants live in services outside the data they protect, so any code can put an entity into an invalid state; a rich model keeps rules in entity methods, which pays off only when the domain has real rules and not for plain CRUD.
- architecture-02 | architecture | middle | open | Asks how organising code by vertical feature slices differs from organising it by technical layers, and what each choice does to the files touched by a typical change. | Layer folders spread one feature across every layer so a change touches many places and couples features through shared layer abstractions, while vertical slices keep a feature's request, logic and data access together and let each slice choose its own complexity, at the cost of possible duplication between slices.
- architecture-03 | architecture | middle | single | Asks which listed benefit requires microservices and cannot be obtained from a well-built modular monolith. | Enforced module boundaries, per-module data schemas and team ownership are all achievable inside a modular monolith, but deploying and scaling one module independently of the others needs separate deployable services.
- architecture-04 | architecture | middle | multi | Asks the reader to select which responsibilities belong in an application service (use case handler) and which belong in the domain model. | An application service orchestrates a use case - loads the aggregate through a repository, calls its domain methods, commits the unit of work and maps results to DTOs - while business invariants and decisions belong in the domain entities and domain services.
- architecture-05 | architecture | middle | find-bug | A BCL-only Order aggregate enforces a maximum total in AddLine, but the caller changes a line's quantity directly and the program prints a total above the limit; the reader clicks the line that lets the invariant be bypassed. | The public setter on OrderLine.Quantity lets code change a child entity without going through the aggregate root, so the root never re-checks its invariant; the fix is to make the line's quantity changeable only through a root method such as Order.ChangeQuantity.
- architecture-06 | architecture | senior | multi | Asks the reader to select the true statements about context map relationships such as conformist, anti-corruption layer, open host service, published language and shared kernel. | A conformist downstream adopts the upstream model as is, an anti-corruption layer translates it to protect the downstream model, an open host service with a published language offers one well-documented protocol to many consumers, and a shared kernel is a small jointly owned model that both teams must change together.
- architecture-07 | architecture | senior | single | Given an Order aggregate with OrderLine children and a Customer aggregate, asks which set of repositories a DDD design should define. | Repositories are defined only for aggregate roots (Order and Customer), because child entities such as OrderLine are loaded and saved through their root, and a repository per table would let code modify children outside the aggregate's consistency boundary.
- architecture-08 | architecture | senior | open | Asks how to handle a user who submits a command and then immediately sees stale data because the read model is updated asynchronously, and what the options cost. | With an asynchronously projected read model a read right after a write can miss it, so the design must choose deliberately: return the result or version from the command and update the UI optimistically, wait or poll until the projection reaches that version, read that one view from the write side, or tell the user the change is processing.
- architecture-09 | architecture | senior | open | Asks whether domain entities in a clean or DDD-style .NET application can be mapped directly by EF Core or need separate persistence models, and what EF Core features make direct mapping workable. | EF Core can map domain entities without attributes through Fluent API configuration in the infrastructure layer, private setters, backing fields for encapsulated collections and parameterised constructors, so a separate persistence model is usually unnecessary duplication unless the domain model and the schema really diverge.
- architecture-10 | architecture | lead | situation | A senior engineer proposes storing the state of every service as an event stream starting with the next project, and the tech lead must decide and set the scope. | Event sourcing pays off only where an audit trail, temporal queries or rebuilding projections are real requirements, and it brings event schema versioning, replay and snapshot handling, eventual consistency and a learning curve, so the lead limits it to a pilot in one justified bounded context with an ADR and exit criteria rather than a system-wide mandate.
- aspnet-core-01 | aspnet-core | junior | single | In a MapPost handler with a parameter of a custom class type and no binding attribute, where does ASP.NET Core 10 take its value from? | Minimal APIs bind a complex-type parameter that is not a registered service and has no TryParse or BindAsync from the JSON request body by default, while simple types come from the route or query string.
- aspnet-core-02 | aspnet-core | middle | find-bug | Find the line in a convention-based middleware class that injects a scoped DbContext through its constructor, so that one instance is shared across requests or startup fails scope validation. | Convention-based middleware is constructed once for the application lifetime, so scoped services must be taken as parameters of InvokeAsync, not of the constructor.
- aspnet-core-03 | aspnet-core | middle | single | Which attribute lets you apply an MVC filter that has constructor dependencies to an action without registering the filter type in the DI container? | TypeFilterAttribute creates the filter with ActivatorUtilities and needs no registration, whereas ServiceFilterAttribute resolves the filter from DI and fails if the type is not registered.
- aspnet-core-04 | aspnet-core | middle | multi | Which statements about keyed services in Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection (.NET 8 and later) are true? | Keyed services are registered with AddKeyedSingleton, AddKeyedScoped or AddKeyedTransient and resolved with [FromKeyedServices] or GetRequiredKeyedService, and a keyed registration is not returned when the same type is resolved without a key.
- aspnet-core-05 | aspnet-core | senior | open | How do you read the request body in a logging middleware without breaking model binding later in the pipeline, and what does it cost? | The request body is a forward-only stream, so the middleware must call Request.EnableBuffering, read the body, reset Position to 0 before calling next, and accept the extra memory and disk buffering for large bodies.
- aspnet-core-06 | aspnet-core | senior | single | A singleton is registered with a factory lambda that resolves a scoped service, and ValidateOnBuild does not report it at startup: why? | ValidateOnBuild analyses only the constructor call sites the container can see, so a factory delegate is opaque to it, and the problem surfaces only when the factory runs and ValidateScopes rejects resolving a scoped service from the root.
- aspnet-core-07 | aspnet-core | senior | multi | Which statements about how ConfigurationBinder binds a configuration section to an options class are true? | Binding is case-insensitive, leaves properties at their defaults when keys are missing, ignores keys that match no property unless ErrorOnUnknownConfiguration is set, and skips non-public setters unless BindNonPublicProperties is enabled.
- aspnet-core-08 | aspnet-core | senior | situation | A singleton cache turns out to have two instances with different contents, and Program.cs calls services.BuildServiceProvider() to resolve a dependency while registering other services: what do you do? | Calling BuildServiceProvider during registration creates a second container with its own singletons (analyzer warning ASP0000), so the fix is to defer resolution with factory overloads or IConfigureOptions<T> instead of building a provider early.
- aspnet-core-09 | aspnet-core | lead | open | A team proposes moving business validation and database transaction handling into MVC action filters so that controllers stay thin: how do you decide and what rule do you set? | Filters fit HTTP-level cross-cutting concerns, but business rules and transaction boundaries placed there become invisible, MVC-only and untestable outside the pipeline, so they belong in the application layer, with filters limited to mapping and HTTP concerns.
- aspnet-core-10 | aspnet-core | lead | open | The team debates exposing Kestrel directly to the internet versus putting a reverse proxy in front: what criteria and risks decide it? | Kestrel is supported as an edge server, so a reverse proxy is justified by concrete needs such as sharing an IP and port across apps, central TLS and certificate handling, extra filtering or load balancing, at the cost of an extra component and forwarded-header configuration.
- aspnet-core-11 | aspnet-core | lead | situation | A developer's pull request replaces the built-in DI container with a third-party container to get assembly scanning and decorators across the solution: how do you handle it? | The built-in container covers most needs, including keyed services since .NET 8, so a replacement is accepted only for features the team actually needs, weighed against an extra dependency, different lifetime and disposal semantics and onboarding cost, and recorded as a team decision.
- aspnet-core-12 | aspnet-core | architect | open | Across a platform of services, should background processing run as hosted services inside the API hosts or in dedicated worker hosts, and what trade-offs hold over years? | In-process hosted services share the API's scaling, deployments and shutdown budget, so work runs once per instance and competes with requests, while dedicated Worker Service hosts scale and deploy independently at the cost of more deployables and an explicit hand-off such as a queue.
- async-01 | async | junior | single | Asks when declaring an async method with a void return type is appropriate and what goes wrong elsewhere. | async void is meant only for event handlers because the caller gets no task to await, cannot know when the method finishes and cannot catch its exceptions, which go straight to the synchronization context or thread pool.
- async-02 | async | middle | output | Asks what a program prints when the first task to finish in Task.WhenAny is faulted (completed via TaskCompletionSource.SetException) and the code prints whether the winner is that task and its Status. | await Task.WhenAny never throws for a faulted input: it returns the completed task itself, so the output is the reference check True and the status Faulted, and the error surfaces only when the winner is awaited.
- async-03 | async | middle | output | Asks what a .NET 10 program prints when it awaits a faulted non-generic Task with ConfigureAwait(ConfigureAwaitOptions.SuppressThrowing) inside try/catch and then prints the task status. | Since .NET 8 the SuppressThrowing option makes the await complete without rethrowing the stored exception, so the catch block is skipped and the program prints the Faulted status.
- async-04 | async | middle | multi | Asks which expressions can be used with await, mixing Task, ValueTask, Task.Yield(), a custom type with an extension GetAwaiter, an IAsyncResult and a Thread. | await works with any type that has an accessible GetAwaiter method (instance or extension) returning an awaiter with IsCompleted, GetResult and INotifyCompletion.OnCompleted, so being a Task is not required and IAsyncResult or Thread are not awaitable.
- async-05 | async | senior | output | Asks what a program prints when the caller sets an AsyncLocal<string> value, an awaited async method changes it after await Task.Yield() and prints it, and the caller prints it again afterwards. | The ExecutionContext flows down into the async method, but a change made inside the method is restored when its state machine returns, so the callee prints its new value while the caller still sees the original one.
- async-06 | async | senior | find-bug | Asks for the line that makes an IAsyncEnumerable iterator ignore the token passed through WithCancellation, so the consumer that cancels after two items still receives all of them. | A token passed via WithCancellation reaches the iterator only through a CancellationToken parameter marked [EnumeratorCancellation]; without the attribute the parameter keeps its default value and the iterator never sees the cancellation.
- async-07 | async | lead | single | Asks which team standard to adopt for classes that need asynchronous initialization, given developers currently call .Result in constructors or start async void Init methods. | Constructors cannot await, so the sound standard is a private constructor plus a static async factory method (or an explicitly awaited initialization task), because blocking in the constructor risks deadlocks and async void Init hides failures and completion.
- async-08 | async | lead | open | Asks what policy a lead sets for fire-and-forget tasks in a service after errors from discarded tasks were silently lost for weeks. | An exception in a task nobody awaits is only raised through TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException and is not rethrown, so the policy requires every background operation to be owned and observed, for example by a hosted queue service or a helper that logs failures, with discards of task results flagged in review and by analyzers.
- async-09 | async | architect | open | Asks how an architect decides whether converting a fleet of synchronous I/O-bound services to async end to end is worth the multi-year effort and what it will and will not improve. | Async I/O raises throughput per instance by not holding threads during waits, which matters for high-concurrency I/O-bound services, but it does not reduce the latency of a single request or help CPU-bound work, so the decision rests on measured concurrency, thread usage and blocking hot spots rather than on expected speed-ups.
- behavioral-01 | behavioral | middle | situation | A manager asks you to fix a customer's broken records right now by running a hand-written UPDATE directly against the production database; what do you do? | Neither refuse nor run untested ad-hoc SQL alone: script the change, test it on a copy, have a second person review it, run it inside a transaction that checks the affected row count, take a backup or before-image first, and record it in a ticket.
- behavioral-02 | behavioral | middle | single | A colleague whose production access request is still pending asks to use your credentials for an urgent fix; which response is best? | Do not share credentials, because that breaks accountability and least privilege; instead help unblock them by speeding up the access request or doing the work yourself under your own account while they guide you.
- behavioral-03 | behavioral | middle | multi | Your feature has been blocked for a week by another team that has not answered your request for an API change; which actions are appropriate? | Appropriate actions are a specific request with the deadline impact in the other team's official channel, escalation with facts through your own lead, and offering a workaround or a contribution to their code; writing to their database directly or silently waiting are not.
- behavioral-04 | behavioral | middle | situation | While debugging you notice that another team's service writes customers' full personal and payment details into shared logs; what do you do? | A possible personal data breach triggers a formal process with legal deadlines (under the GDPR, 72 hours for the controller to notify the authority), so report it at once to the owning team and the security or privacy contact, and do not copy or spread the data as evidence.
- behavioral-05 | behavioral | middle | open | You are assigned a task with a deadline in a technology you have never used, for example a Python data pipeline; how do you handle it? | Name the knowledge gap when you accept the task so that the estimate and plan include learning time, timebox the learning, and arrange review or pairing with someone experienced instead of hiding the gap.
- behavioral-06 | behavioral | senior | single | You found an exploitable vulnerability in an open-source NuGet package your product depends on; what is the best first step? | Report it privately through the project's security policy or private vulnerability reporting, and mitigate it in your own product in parallel; a public issue with a proof of concept exposes every user before a fix exists.
- behavioral-07 | behavioral | senior | situation | You notice that a respected teammate regularly pastes code from GPL-licensed projects into the company's closed-source product; what do you do? | Distributing a proprietary product that contains GPL code creates obligations the company may not be able to meet, so raise it privately with the teammate first, then bring in the lead and legal to audit and replace the code, rather than ignoring it or shaming the teammate publicly.
- behavioral-08 | behavioral | senior | situation | After an outage caused by your team's bug, an account manager asks you to tell the customer it was caused by their own misconfiguration; how do you respond? | Refuse to state a falsehood and offer an honest alternative instead: a factual, blameless incident summary with the cause, the impact and the remediation, agreed with management.
- behavioral-09 | behavioral | senior | situation | A teammate confides that their change quietly corrupted some customer records and asks you not to tell anyone while they fix it; what do you do? | Harm to users outweighs the promise of secrecy, so push the teammate to report it themselves now, offer to help, and make clear that you will raise it if they do not, framing it as a blameless issue rather than a punishment.
- behavioral-10 | behavioral | senior | situation | Your team lead left suddenly, and you are informally expected to run planning, handle stakeholders and still deliver your own tasks; what do you do? | Make the arrangement explicit with management (scope, decision authority, duration, what is dropped from your own work) instead of silently absorbing both roles until something fails.
- behavioral-11 | behavioral | senior | open | You are asked to build a large feature you believe users will not use; how do you raise and act on that doubt? | Treat the doubt as a hypothesis: bring data to the product owner, who owns value, and propose the cheapest experiment (a prototype or a feature-flagged slice), then accept the owner's decision.
- behavioral-12 | behavioral | lead | situation | Senior management mandates a change your team and you oppose, and you must announce it and lead its rollout; how do you handle it? | Voice your disagreement upward with evidence, then present the decision to the team with its real reasoning and own it, rather than blaming management with "it's not my call", while collecting the team's concerns to feed back.
- behavioral-13 | behavioral | architect | open | Product teams routinely ignore the architecture guidelines you publish; how do you regain influence without simply issuing mandates? | Influence comes from making the recommended way the easiest one (templates, paved paths) and from shaping decisions together with the teams through an advice process and shared decision records, not from top-down rules enforced from an ivory tower.
- blazor-01 | blazor | junior | single | How does a parent component pass a value to a child component, and what must the child declare to receive it? | The child exposes a public property marked with [Parameter], and the parent sets it as an attribute with the same name in its markup.
- blazor-02 | blazor | junior | single | Why does an EditForm whose model has [Required] attributes submit without any validation messages? | EditForm checks DataAnnotations attributes only when a DataAnnotationsValidator component is placed inside it; without it, the attributes are ignored.
- blazor-03 | blazor | middle | find-bug | Find the line that throws when a prerendered InteractiveServer component calls IJSRuntime in OnInitializedAsync. | During prerendering there is no browser connection, so JS interop calls fail; they belong in OnAfterRenderAsync when firstRender is true.
- blazor-04 | blazor | middle | open | Why does a prerendered interactive component load its data twice and show a flicker, and how do you avoid it? | With prerendering the component is created once for the static HTML and again when it becomes interactive, so OnInitializedAsync runs twice unless state is carried over with PersistentComponentState or prerendering is disabled.
- blazor-05 | blazor | middle | single | Why does the parent re-render after a child invokes an EventCallback parameter but not after it invokes an Action parameter? | EventCallback dispatches through the receiving component's IHandleEvent, so ComponentBase calls StateHasChanged on the parent; a plain Action delegate bypasses that.
- blazor-06 | blazor | middle | single | In a .NET 8 or later Blazor Web App a page renders but its @onclick button does nothing; what is the most likely cause? | A component with no render mode and no global interactivity is rendered with static SSR, which produces plain HTML with no event handlers attached.
- blazor-07 | blazor | middle | multi | Which statements about ProtectedLocalStorage and ProtectedSessionStorage are true? | They encrypt data with ASP.NET Core Data Protection on the server, work only in server-side interactive rendering, are asynchronous and cannot be used during prerendering.
- blazor-08 | blazor | middle | multi | Which statements about OnSubmit, OnValidSubmit, Model and EditContext on an EditForm are true? | OnValidSubmit runs only after validation passes, OnSubmit requires calling EditContext.Validate yourself, and combining OnSubmit with OnValidSubmit or Model with EditContext throws.
- blazor-09 | blazor | senior | situation | An InteractiveServer app runs out of memory and drops users as concurrent sessions grow; how do you diagnose and fix it? | Every circuit keeps its component tree and scoped services in server memory, including retained disconnected circuits, so you shrink per-circuit state, tune circuit retention, scale out with sticky sessions and measure memory per circuit.
- blazor-10 | blazor | senior | find-bug | Find the line that leaks memory when a component passes DotNetObjectReference.Create(this) to JavaScript in OnAfterRenderAsync. | A DotNetObjectReference keeps the .NET object alive until it is disposed, so creating one on every render without a firstRender check and without Dispose leaks references.
- blazor-11 | blazor | senior | single | Why does a child component re-render every time its parent re-renders even though the object passed as its parameter did not change? | ComponentBase skips re-rendering only when all parameters are of known immutable primitive types with unchanged values; any parameter of a complex type is treated as possibly changed.
- blazor-12 | blazor | senior | multi | Which pieces are required for an EditForm on a static SSR page in .NET 8 or later to post and bind its model? | The form needs a FormName, the model property needs [SupplyParameterFromForm], and the pipeline needs antiforgery middleware; an interactive render mode is not required.
- blazor-13 | blazor | senior | open | How do you design data access for a component that runs in InteractiveAuto mode? | The same component first runs on the server and later in WebAssembly, so it depends on an interface with a server implementation that uses the database directly and a client implementation that calls a web API over HttpClient.
- blazor-14 | blazor | senior | open | Which user state survives a page reload, a new tab or a long network drop in an InteractiveServer app, and where should state live that must survive them? | In-memory circuit state lives only as long as the circuit, so a reload, a new tab or an expired disconnected circuit loses it; durable state goes to a database, browser storage or the URL.
- blazor-15 | blazor | senior | open | What happens to an InteractiveServer circuit when a component throws, and what can and cannot ErrorBoundary contain? | An unhandled exception is fatal to the circuit; ErrorBoundary catches exceptions from rendering and lifecycle methods of its child content but not exceptions from code outside the renderer such as timer callbacks.
- blazor-16 | blazor | senior | multi | Which statements about JavaScript interop in the InteractiveServer render mode are true? | Every interop call is an asynchronous round trip over SignalR, IJSInProcessRuntime is not available, and large payloads are limited by the hub message size, so streams are used for big data.
- blazor-17 | blazor | lead | situation | A Blazor Web App has public content pages and an admin area, and the team argues about global versus per-page interactivity; how do you decide and set the rule? | Per-page or per-component interactivity keeps content pages as cheap static SSR without circuits or WebAssembly downloads, while global interactivity is needed only when layout components must be interactive everywhere.
- blazor-18 | blazor | lead | open | Several teams want a shared Blazor component library; which rules and process do you set so it stays usable for years? | Components in a Razor class library must not assume a render mode or hosting model, ship with versioning and a deprecation policy, and keep CSS and JS isolated, so consumers can upgrade independently.
- blazor-19 | blazor | lead | open | What team policy do you set for using third-party JavaScript libraries from Blazor components? | Each library is wrapped once in a typed C# service or component that loads an isolated JS module, disposes its object references and works in every render mode, instead of scattered string-named interop calls.
- blazor-20 | blazor | lead | situation | Validation rules for WebAssembly forms and the backing API have drifted apart and caused bad data; what do you change? | Client validation in WebAssembly is only a convenience because the code runs on the user's machine, so the API must validate every request, and rules are shared from one library used by both sides.
- blazor-21 | blazor | architect | situation | An InteractiveServer app built for one office must now serve users on several continents; how do you redesign hosting and render modes? | InteractiveServer pays network latency on every UI event and needs a live connection to the region holding the circuit, so for distant users you move interaction to WebAssembly or static SSR and deploy per region.
- blazor-22 | blazor | architect | open | How do you decide between Blazor and a JavaScript SPA framework for a product expected to live many years? | The decision weighs shared C# code and team skills against WebAssembly download size, the ecosystem of UI components and the hiring market, and it is made per product surface rather than for the whole company.
- cloud-containers-01 | cloud-containers | junior | single | A framework-dependent ASP.NET Core app fails to start on mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/runtime:10.0; which official base image should the final stage use? | The runtime image contains only the .NET runtime, while the aspnet image adds the ASP.NET Core shared framework that a framework-dependent web app needs; runtime-deps fits only self-contained apps and sdk is for building.
- cloud-containers-02 | cloud-containers | junior | open | What do a Pod, a Deployment and a Service each do when a .NET API runs in Kubernetes? | A Pod runs the containers, a Deployment keeps the desired number of Pod replicas and rolls out new versions, and a Service gives a stable address that load-balances across the matching Pods whose IPs keep changing.
- cloud-containers-03 | cloud-containers | junior | multi | Which Azure and AWS services run a .NET container image without the team managing servers or a cluster's nodes? | Azure Container Apps and Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate run containers on managed infrastructure, while Azure Virtual Machines and plain EC2 instances leave the OS and runtime host to the team.
- cloud-containers-04 | cloud-containers | middle | single | How is the value of a Kubernetes Secret protected by default? | Secret values are only base64-encoded and stored unencrypted in etcd unless encryption at rest is configured, so anyone with API read access to the Secret or access to etcd can read them.
- cloud-containers-05 | cloud-containers | middle | open | What does Kubernetes do when a liveness, a readiness or a startup probe of a .NET container fails? | A failed readiness probe removes the Pod from Service endpoints without a restart, a failed liveness probe makes the kubelet restart the container, and a startup probe holds off the other probes until the app has started.
- cloud-containers-06 | cloud-containers | middle | open | What does dotnet publish with the PublishContainer target do in the .NET 8 SDK, and when do you still need a Dockerfile? | Since .NET 8 the SDK builds an OCI image directly from the publish output and picks the base image from the project type, but it cannot run arbitrary build commands like a Dockerfile RUN step, so extra OS packages or custom steps still need a Dockerfile.
- cloud-containers-07 | cloud-containers | middle | multi | Which statements about the Ubuntu chiseled .NET container images are true? | Chiseled images have no shell and no package manager and run as a non-root user, so they are smaller with a smaller attack surface, but you cannot apt install or exec a shell into them for debugging.
- cloud-containers-08 | cloud-containers | middle | find-bug | In a Dockerfile that restores from a private NuGet feed, find the line that leaks the feed token into the published image. | A token passed through ARG or ENV is recorded in the image metadata or layers and can be read with docker history or inspect; a BuildKit secret mount (RUN --mount=type=secret) exposes it only during that RUN step.
- cloud-containers-09 | cloud-containers | middle | open | How does an ASP.NET Core app hosted in Azure read secrets from Key Vault without any credential stored in its configuration? | The app gets a managed identity that Azure issues tokens for, DefaultAzureCredential picks it up, and the Key Vault configuration provider loads secrets into IConfiguration, so no client secret or password exists in files or variables.
- cloud-containers-10 | cloud-containers | middle | single | Where should a .NET AWS Lambda function create its HttpClient and database client so warm invocations do not pay for them again? | Objects created outside the handler method, in a static field or the function constructor, live in the execution environment and are reused by later invocations, while objects created inside the handler are rebuilt on every call.
- cloud-containers-11 | cloud-containers | senior | single | What GC heap limit does a .NET app get by default when its container has a memory limit and no GC heap limit is configured? | Since .NET Core 3.0 the runtime detects the container memory limit and sets the GC heap hard limit to the larger of 20 MB and 75% of that limit, leaving room for native memory.
- cloud-containers-12 | cloud-containers | senior | find-bug | In a Deployment manifest and health check setup for a .NET API, find the line that makes every Pod restart in a loop during a short database outage. | The liveness probe points at a health endpoint that checks the database, so a shared dependency failure restarts all healthy processes; dependency checks belong in the readiness probe and liveness should check only the process itself.
- cloud-containers-13 | cloud-containers | senior | find-bug | An app with reloadOnChange never sees ConfigMap edits to appsettings.json mounted into the container; find the manifest line that prevents the update. | A ConfigMap mounted with subPath is copied once and never receives updates, while a whole-volume mount is refreshed by the kubelet through a symlink swap that the file watcher can see.
- cloud-containers-14 | cloud-containers | senior | situation | A .NET API in Kubernetes with a CPU limit of 1 shows p99 latency spikes while average CPU usage stays at 40%; what do you check and change? | The CPU limit is enforced as a CFS quota per period, so bursts get throttled even at low average usage, and the runtime sizes the thread pool and GC from the limit-derived ProcessorCount; check throttling metrics, then raise or remove the CPU limit and size requests instead.
- cloud-containers-15 | cloud-containers | senior | situation | Every rolling update of a .NET service produces a burst of 502 errors at the ingress even though the app handles SIGTERM gracefully; what is going on and how do you fix it? | Removing the Pod from endpoints and sending SIGTERM happen in parallel, so traffic still arrives after Kestrel stops accepting; a preStop delay lets routing catch up, and terminationGracePeriodSeconds must cover the delay plus the host shutdown timeout.
- cloud-containers-16 | cloud-containers | senior | single | A HorizontalPodAutoscaler with a 70% CPU utilization target never scales a Deployment whose containers set no CPU requests; why? | Utilization is calculated as a percentage of the containers' CPU requests, so without requests the HPA cannot compute the metric and takes no scaling action for it.
- cloud-containers-17 | cloud-containers | senior | open | How should a .NET queue-processing worker in containers be autoscaled, and why does CPU-based scaling serve it poorly? | An I/O-bound consumer can have a growing backlog at low CPU, so it should scale on queue length or lag through event-driven rules such as KEDA or Container Apps scale rules, with a replica cap set by what downstream systems can absorb.
- cloud-containers-18 | cloud-containers | senior | single | Which disruptions does a PodDisruptionBudget with minAvailable: 2 protect a three-replica .NET service from? | A PodDisruptionBudget only limits voluntary disruptions that go through the Eviction API, such as node drains during upgrades, and does nothing against involuntary ones like a node crash or an OOM kill.
- cloud-containers-19 | cloud-containers | senior | multi | Which securityContext settings harden a Pod that runs an ASP.NET Core container? | runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem with a writable emptyDir for temp files, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false and dropping all capabilities reduce privilege, while privileged: true or hostNetwork widen it.
- cloud-containers-20 | cloud-containers | lead | situation | A team of six without a platform engineer wants to move five .NET services to AKS because Kubernetes is the industry standard; how do you decide the hosting? | The decision weighs operational ownership against control: a self-run AKS cluster brings upgrades, networking and security work that a small team must staff, while Container Apps or App Service cover the actual requirements with far less operational risk unless a concrete need demands the Kubernetes API.
- cloud-containers-21 | cloud-containers | lead | open | What policy should a team set for .NET base image tags and rebuilds so production images get security patches without surprise changes? | Version tags like aspnet:10.0 move with every patch while digests never change, so the team pins a digest or exact version for reproducibility and runs automated, tested rebuilds when new patched base images ship instead of relying on ad-hoc rebuilds.
- cloud-containers-22 | cloud-containers | lead | situation | Two months after enabling autoscaling the cloud bill for your services has doubled and finance asks the lead for an explanation and a plan; what do you do? | First attribute cost by resource tags and scaling events, then fix the causes such as oversized requests, missing replica caps or scale-in that never happens, and set budgets and alerts with clear ownership so cost becomes a tracked engineering metric.

- oop-solid-10 | oop-solid | senior | situation | An IRepository with 25 methods is implemented by six classes, half of which throw NotImplementedException, and every change to it forces edits and rebuilds in unrelated modules; what do you do? | NotImplementedException in implementations signals both an ISP violation and broken substitutability, so the fix is to split the interface into role interfaces by what each client actually calls and migrate clients incrementally.

- oop-solid-15 | oop-solid | architect | open | A platform team ships BaseController, BaseService and BaseEntity classes that thirty services must inherit from; why does this become a liability over years and what would you offer instead? | Inheritance at platform scale turns the fragile base class problem into an organisation-wide coupling where any change to base class internals can break every service, so cross-cutting behaviour should be offered through composition (middleware, decorators, small interfaces and helpers) with few deliberate extension points.

- testing-01 | testing | junior | single | Which of several ways to write a test that checks a discount for many inputs follows the guidance against logic such as if, loops and computed expectations inside a test body? | A test with branches, loops or an expected value computed by the same formula as the production code can hide its own bug, so expectations should be literal values and cases should be separate tests or parameterized rows.
- testing-02 | testing | middle | find-bug | A hand-written ExpectThrows helper calls an async method that throws ArgumentException but prints FAIL: no exception; find the line in the helper that lets the exception escape notice. | The helper invokes the Func<Task> without awaiting it, and an async method stores its exception in the returned task, so the helper must await the task (as Assert.ThrowsAsync does) to observe the exception.

- testing-04 | testing | middle | multi | Which statements about Playwright for .NET actionability checks and web-first assertions are true when replacing Thread.Sleep in browser end-to-end tests? | Playwright actions wait for the element to be actionable and Expect assertions retry until the condition holds or the timeout expires, so fixed sleeps are unnecessary and make tests both slower and flakier.
- testing-05 | testing | senior | find-bug | A test of a background consumer polls with a WaitUntil helper and prints PASS although the consumer never processes the message; find the defective line in the helper. | The polling helper simply returns when the timeout elapses instead of failing, so the test passes without the condition ever becoming true; a wait-for-condition helper must throw or fail on timeout.
- testing-06 | testing | senior | open | Why is mocking a third-party SDK client directly in unit tests risky, and what structure do you use instead? | A mock of a type you do not own encodes your assumptions about its behaviour, so you wrap the SDK in your own narrow adapter interface, mock or fake that interface, and cover the adapter with integration tests against the real dependency.
- testing-07 | testing | senior | open | How do outside-in and inside-out TDD differ in where you start and how you use test doubles, and when would you choose each? | Outside-in starts from a failing acceptance test and uses mocks to discover the interfaces of collaborators top-down, while inside-out builds and state-verifies the core units first and composes them later, trading design discovery against coupling of tests to interactions.
- testing-08 | testing | senior | multi | Which techniques make a test of an asynchronous message consumer deterministic instead of relying on sleeps? | The test should wait on an explicit completion signal such as a TaskCompletionSource set by the code or a fake, bounded with Task.WaitAsync(timeout), rather than on Thread.Sleep, Task.Delay or blocking .Result calls.
- testing-09 | testing | senior | single | How do you test endpoints protected by [Authorize] with WebApplicationFactory without a real identity provider? | In ConfigureTestServices you register a test AuthenticationHandler scheme that issues a ClaimsPrincipal with the needed claims and make it the default scheme, so the real authorization policies still run.
- testing-10 | testing | lead | situation | The team must change billing rules in an old module that has no tests and tangled dependencies, and a bug would cost money; how do you lead the work? | First pin current behaviour with characterization tests at a seam you can reach, break dependencies with minimal safe refactorings, then change behaviour test-first, instead of either rewriting blindly or editing without a safety net.
- testing-11 | testing | lead | situation | A browser end-to-end suite now takes two hours and gates every pull request, so developers batch changes and wait; what do you do as tech lead? | Push most checks down to unit and integration tests that verify the same rules faster, keep only a thin set of critical-journey end-to-end tests on the gate, and run the rest on a schedule, because end-to-end tests are the most expensive way to find a defect.
- testing-12 | testing | lead | open | Part of the team wants to make TDD mandatory for all code and the rest objects; how do you decide and introduce it? | TDD is a skill whose benefit depends on context, so a lead grows it through pairing, katas and pilot areas where it fits and judges it by outcomes such as defect rates and design feedback, rather than mandating test-first for every line or policing it by a metric.
- testing-13 | testing | architect | open | Dozens of teams write their own fakes of a shared platform service and their tests pass while production breaks; how do you organise test doubles across the organisation for years? | The owning team ships an official in-memory fake together with the client library and runs the same contract test suite against both the fake and the real service, so the fake cannot silently drift and consumers stop maintaining divergent copies.
- types-memory-01 | types-memory | junior | output | A struct with an int field and an int[] field is assigned to a second variable; the code changes the int field and an array element through the copy and then prints both from the original, and the question asks for the output. | Copying a struct copies its fields, and for the array field that copies only the reference, so the original sees the array element change (9) but keeps its own int field (1), printing "1 9".
- types-memory-02 | types-memory | middle | output | An int is boxed into object and then unboxed with an explicit cast to long, and the question asks what happens at run time. | Unboxing must target the exact boxed value type (or its nullable form), so casting a boxed int directly to long throws System.InvalidCastException instead of performing a numeric conversion.
- types-memory-03 | types-memory | middle | output | Code assigns to a field of a struct element through a List<T> indexer, for example points[0].X = 5, after doing the same through an array, and the question asks for the result. | The List<T> indexer returns a copy of the struct (a value, not a variable), so assigning to its field is compile error CS1612, while the same write through an array element compiles because an array access is a variable.
- types-memory-04 | types-memory | middle | find-bug | A word counter stores a mutable struct Stats as Dictionary<string, Stats> values, reads the value into a local, increments its count and never writes it back, so the program prints 0 instead of 3; find the defective line. | Reading a struct value from a Dictionary returns a copy, so incrementing the local does not change the stored entry; the fix is to write the value back or update in place with CollectionsMarshal.GetValueRefOrAddDefault.
- types-memory-05 | types-memory | senior | output | Unsafe.SizeOf is printed for a struct with fields byte, long, byte in default layout and for the same struct marked [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Auto)], and the question asks for the two sizes. | C# structs use sequential layout by default, so alignment padding around the 8-byte long gives 24 bytes, while LayoutKind.Auto lets the runtime reorder the fields and gives 16 bytes, printing "24 16".
- types-memory-06 | types-memory | senior | output | Over the array {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}, span.Slice(0, 4).CopyTo(span.Slice(1)) shifts the elements right inside the same array, and the question asks what the array prints. | Span<T>.CopyTo copies the whole source correctly even when source and destination overlap, as memmove does, so the result is "1 1 2 3 4" rather than the "1 1 1 1 1" a naive forward loop would produce.
- types-memory-07 | types-memory | senior | multi | Given several operations on a small struct in a hot path on .NET 10, the question asks which of them allocate a box on the heap. | Passing the struct to a parameter of an interface type and calling GetType() on it both box, while a call through a generic method constrained with where T : IFoo and string interpolation with the C# 10 interpolated string handler do not box.
- types-memory-08 | types-memory | lead | single | The team wants one coding rule for stackalloc in shared code, and the question asks which proposed rule to adopt. | Allow stackalloc only for a small constant maximum size (for example 1024 bytes) outside loops and fall back to a heap or ArrayPool buffer above it, because stack space is limited, a stackalloc buffer lives until the method returns, and an input-sized stackalloc can overflow the stack.
- types-memory-09 | types-memory | lead | situation | A developer opens a large pull request that rewrites the order-file parser with Span<T>, stackalloc, MemoryMarshal and unsafe pointers, claims it is faster, and only that developer understands the code; what does the lead do? | Accept such code only with a benchmark that proves a meaningful gain on a measured hot path, prefer safe Span<T> APIs over unsafe and MemoryMarshal, isolate any unsafe code in a small module with boundary and fuzz tests, and require a second reviewer who understands it.
- types-memory-10 | types-memory | lead | open | Should an internal library used by many teams add ReadOnlySpan<char> and Memory<T> overloads next to its string and array APIs, and which rules decide the parameter type of each method? | Add span overloads for synchronous hot-path methods while keeping the string and array ones for convenience, and use Memory<T> or ReadOnlyMemory<T> for async or stored data, because a span cannot cross await or be stored on the heap and every public overload is permanent API surface.
- types-memory-11 | types-memory | architect | open | How do you design buffer ownership for a zero-copy message pipeline that passes pooled buffers through decoding, validation and persistence components owned by different teams over years? | Make ownership explicit with a single owner at a time, transferred through IMemoryOwner<T> and released exactly once, give consumers only Memory<T> or Span<T> leases scoped to a call, and copy at component and async boundaries where ownership cannot be enforced, because a Memory<T> over a returned pooled buffer silently corrupts data.
- types-memory-12 | types-memory | architect | single | A service must keep tens of millions of small fixed-size price records in memory for years of growth with minimal GC cost, and the question asks which representation to choose. | A large array of structs without reference fields, indexed by key, is a few heap objects whose contents the GC does not need to trace, while millions of class instances are each separate objects that every full collection must mark.
- ui-dotnet-01 | ui-dotnet | junior | open | Asks what the model, the view and the view model each do in a WPF, WinUI or Avalonia app and how they talk to each other. | The view model exposes state and commands without referencing the view, and the view connects to it only through data binding and commands, which makes the view model testable without a UI.
- ui-dotnet-02 | ui-dotnet | middle | find-bug | A runnable view model prints property names from PropertyChanged; FullName depends on FirstName and LastName, but the setters never report FullName, so the user must find the line where the dependent notification is missing. | A computed property has no setter of its own, so the setters of the properties it depends on must also raise PropertyChanged for it, otherwise bindings to it never refresh.
- ui-dotnet-03 | ui-dotnet | middle | find-bug | A runnable view model whose setter raises PropertyChanged before it assigns the backing field; the subscriber reads the property in the handler and prints the old value, and the user must find the misordered line. | Subscribers re-read the property inside the PropertyChanged handler, so the event must be raised after the backing field holds the new value.
- ui-dotnet-04 | ui-dotnet | middle | single | Asks why a WinUI TextBlock with Text="{x:Bind ViewModel.Status}" never shows updates even though the view model raises PropertyChanged. | The default mode of x:Bind is OneTime, unlike {Binding}, whose default for TextBlock.Text is OneWay, so Mode=OneWay must be set explicitly.
- ui-dotnet-05 | ui-dotnet | middle | single | Asks which property in WPF can be the target of a {Binding} markup extension, with options mixing plain CLR properties of a custom control, INotifyPropertyChanged properties and dependency properties. | The binding target must be a dependency property of a DependencyObject, while the source can be any CLR property; a binding on a plain CLR property of a control fails.
- ui-dotnet-06 | ui-dotnet | middle | single | Asks what happens at run time when a WPF binding path names a property that the DataContext does not have. | No exception is thrown: the binding leaves the target at its fallback or default value and only writes a System.Windows.Data error to the debug trace output, which PresentationTraceSources can make more detailed.
- ui-dotnet-07 | ui-dotnet | middle | multi | Asks which changes made from a Task.Run thread are safe when the data is bound in WPF: setting a scalar view model property, adding to a bound ObservableCollection, adding after EnableCollectionSynchronization, setting TextBox.Text directly, and adding through Dispatcher.InvokeAsync. | WPF marshals PropertyChanged of scalar bound properties to the UI thread, but a CollectionChanged from another thread throws NotSupportedException unless BindingOperations.EnableCollectionSynchronization is used or the change is dispatched, and controls themselves are thread-affine.
- ui-dotnet-08 | ui-dotnet | middle | multi | Asks which statements about compiled bindings in Avalonia 11 are true, covering x:DataType, build-time path checking, reflection use and behaviour without a declared data type. | Compiled bindings need the data type declared with x:DataType, resolve paths at build time so a wrong path is a build error, and avoid reflection-based binding at run time.
- ui-dotnet-09 | ui-dotnet | senior | open | Asks how x:Bind differs from {Binding} in WinUI in where it gets its source, when the binding is resolved and what that means for performance and refactoring. | x:Bind is turned into generated code at compile time and is rooted in the page or control class itself rather than DataContext, so it is type-checked and avoids reflection, but it cannot follow a DataContext set at run time.
- ui-dotnet-10 | ui-dotnet | senior | open | Asks what problem the WPF weak event pattern solves for view models that subscribe to long-lived services and how WeakEventManager changes the reference graph. | A normal event subscription lets the long-lived source keep the listener alive, while WeakEventManager holds the listener through a weak reference so a closed view and its view model can be collected without an explicit unsubscribe.
- ui-dotnet-11 | ui-dotnet | senior | situation | Loading 50,000 search results by calling Add on a bound ObservableCollection in a loop freezes a WPF screen for seconds; how do you diagnose and fix it? | Each Add raises its own CollectionChanged and makes the bound view update item by item, and WPF collection views reject range notifications, so the fix is to build the items first and swap in one new collection with a single PropertyChanged or raise one Reset.
- ui-dotnet-12 | ui-dotnet | senior | open | Asks how the WPF layout system computes element sizes and positions and what makes a property change trigger a new layout pass for part of the tree. | Layout is a recursive two-pass process, Measure then Arrange, and properties marked AffectsMeasure or AffectsArrange invalidate the element so the pass reruns up and down from it, which is why frequent size changes in deep trees are expensive.
- ui-dotnet-13 | ui-dotnet | senior | single | Asks how Avalonia puts its controls on screen on Windows, Linux and macOS and why they look the same on every platform. | Avalonia does not wrap native OS controls; it draws every control itself through its own rendering pipeline, by default with Skia, onto a surface the platform provides.
- ui-dotnet-14 | ui-dotnet | senior | single | Asks why a WPF control property bound OneWay to the view model stops updating after code-behind assigns the property once. | Setting a local value replaces the OneWay binding expression, so later source changes are lost; SetCurrentValue changes the effective value while keeping the binding.
- ui-dotnet-15 | ui-dotnet | lead | open | Asks how a tech lead chooses between hand-written base classes, CommunityToolkit.Mvvm source generators and a reactive framework for a new desktop product built by a team of eight. | The choice weighs boilerplate removal and compile-time generated notification code against the learning curve, debuggability and long-term support of the library, and must be fixed as one team convention rather than mixed per screen.
- ui-dotnet-16 | ui-dotnet | lead | situation | Two teams add styles to merged ResourceDictionaries in one WPF shell's App.xaml and keep breaking each other's screens; what do you change technically and in the process? | Resource lookup walks up to application resources and a duplicate key in merged dictionaries resolves to the last merged one, so ownership, key naming rules and module-scoped dictionaries are needed instead of one global pool.
- ui-dotnet-17 | ui-dotnet | lead | open | Asks how a lead introduces MVVM into a large WPF application whose logic lives in code-behind event handlers, without a feature freeze. | Migrate screen by screen, starting with new and frequently changed screens, extract logic into testable view models behind bindings and commands, and set a rule that new code-behind may only hold view-specific behaviour.
- ui-dotnet-18 | ui-dotnet | lead | situation | Management wants a .NET Framework 4.8 WPF line-of-business app moved to .NET 8 this quarter; how do you assess and plan the move? | WPF on .NET 8 runs only on Windows with a net8.0-windows target, so the risk lies in third-party control suites, unsupported .NET Framework APIs and project-format changes, which call for an inventory and a project-by-project upgrade rather than a big-bang switch.
- ui-dotnet-19 | ui-dotnet | architect | open | Asks how an architect chooses between WPF, WinUI 3 and Avalonia for a line-of-business desktop product that must ship on Windows now, may need Linux and macOS later and will live for ten years. | WPF and WinUI 3 are Windows-only while Avalonia is cross-platform with self-drawn controls, so the decision hinges on platform reach, ecosystem and vendor maturity against migration cost, and a UI-agnostic view model layer keeps the choice reversible.
- ui-dotnet-20 | ui-dotnet | architect | multi | Asks which design decisions keep one view model library reusable across WPF, WinUI and Avalonia front ends. | View models stay portable when they depend only on BCL contracts such as INotifyPropertyChanged, ICommand and ObservableCollection<T>, reach UI services through injected interfaces, and use no framework types such as Visibility, brushes or Application.Current.Dispatcher.
- web-api-01 | web-api | junior | single | A request carries a valid token, but the user lacks permission for the resource: which status code should the API return? | 403 Forbidden means the server understood the credentials and refuses; 401 Unauthorized means credentials are missing or invalid and must come with a WWW-Authenticate challenge.
- web-api-02 | web-api | middle | find-bug | A runnable snippet with a stub handler that returns 404 and a text body parses the body as data and fails; find the line that skips the status check. | HttpClient.GetAsync returns a response for any status code and never throws on 4xx or 5xx, so the code must check IsSuccessStatusCode or call EnsureSuccessStatusCode before reading the body.
- web-api-03 | web-api | middle | single | A client posts an application/xml body to an endpoint that only accepts JSON: which status code fits? | 415 Unsupported Media Type is about the format of the request content, while 406 Not Acceptable is about the Accept header and the response format.
- web-api-04 | web-api | middle | multi | Which of the listed changes to an existing API version break clients that are already integrated? | Removing or renaming a field, changing a field type and making an optional input required are breaking, while adding an optional response field or an optional input is not.
- web-api-05 | web-api | middle | open | Why is an endpoint such as GET /orders/42/cancel dangerous even when only logged-in users can call it? | RFC 9110 defines GET as safe, so crawlers, link prefetchers, caches and automatic retries may issue it without user intent, and any state change it makes is triggered unintentionally.
- web-api-06 | web-api | senior | open | How do you stop two clients that PUT the same resource from silently overwriting each other's changes at the HTTP level? | The server sends an ETag, the client sends it back in If-Match, and the server rejects a stale write with 412 Precondition Failed (and can demand the header with 428 Precondition Required).
- web-api-07 | web-api | senior | open | A list endpoint with page and pageSize slows down on deep pages and shows duplicates while data is inserted: how would you redesign pagination? | Offset pagination makes the database skip rows and shifts pages under inserts, while cursor (keyset) pagination seeks from an opaque continuation token on an indexed key, giving stable and fast pages at the cost of jumping to an arbitrary page.
- web-api-08 | web-api | senior | single | Which exception does a .NET 5+ HttpClient throw when HttpClient.Timeout elapses, and how do you tell it apart from caller cancellation? | It throws TaskCanceledException whose InnerException is TimeoutException, while a cancellation requested by the caller shows up as the caller's token having IsCancellationRequested set.
- web-api-09 | web-api | senior | single | A service downloads large files with GetAsync and then ReadAsStreamAsync, yet memory grows by the file size: what fixes it? | The default HttpCompletionOption.ResponseContentRead buffers the whole body before GetAsync completes, so you must pass ResponseHeadersRead, stream the content and dispose the response.
- web-api-10 | web-api | senior | find-bug | In an ASP.NET Core registration and service class, find the line that makes a typed HttpClient keep calling an old address after a DNS switch. | Typed clients are registered as transient, and injecting one into a singleton pins a single HttpMessageHandler for the process lifetime, so IHttpClientFactory never rotates the handler.
- web-api-11 | web-api | senior | multi | Which statements about AddStandardResilienceHandler from Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Resilience are true for outgoing POST requests? | By default the standard pipeline retries transient failures for every HTTP method including POST, and DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods is needed to stop retries of POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE and CONNECT.
- web-api-12 | web-api | senior | situation | After v2 shipped and DefaultApiVersion was set to 2.0 with AssumeDefaultVersionWhenUnspecified, clients that never send a version started failing: what happened and what do you change? | The assumed default applies to every request without a version, so moving it silently migrates unversioned clients; the default must stay on the oldest supported version or the version must be required explicitly.
- web-api-13 | web-api | lead | open | How do you decide whether your teams write the OpenAPI contract first or generate it from the ASP.NET Core code? | Design-first makes the contract a reviewed artifact that consumers agree on before implementation and that CI can diff for breaking changes, while code-first is faster but lets the contract drift with implementation details.
- web-api-14 | web-api | lead | situation | During a slowdown of a downstream API its traffic multiplied, and each of three services in the call chain retries three times: what do you change and how do you make it a team rule? | Retries at every layer multiply attempts (3 x 3 x 3), so retrying belongs to one layer with a total timeout budget, a circuit breaker and respect for Retry-After.
- web-api-15 | web-api | lead | open | Ten services return errors in ten different shapes and clients parse message text: how do you standardize the error contract? | Adopt RFC 9457 Problem Details everywhere with stable type URIs or error codes that clients branch on, keep detail for humans only, and enforce the shape with shared configuration and contract tests.
- web-api-16 | web-api | architect | situation | Hundreds of partners want push notifications about order changes instead of polling: how do you design outbound webhooks that stay reliable for years? | Webhooks are at-least-once deliveries from a durable queue, so each event needs a unique id for receiver deduplication and a signature, with backoff retries and per-endpoint isolation so one slow partner cannot delay the others.
